parameters.content:
## Publish Approved Article

Last link of the content engine. Iván approves a draft at /admin/drafts/, the
admin service POSTs `{"piece_ids":[1,2]}` here, and this workflow writes the
.njk file to GitHub and marks the piece PUBLISHED. The daily deploy-website.sh
cron picks it up from there — this workflow never touches the live server.

### Before activating

1. **Config node** — set `githubOwner` and `githubRepo` to the real repo.

2. **GitHub credential** — create a *GitHub API* credential named
   `GitHub — triaperformance-docs`, using a fine-grained personal access token
   scoped to that ONE repo with `Contents: Read and write`. Nothing else.
   Then re-select it on both HTTP Request nodes (they show REPLACE_ME).

3. **Postgres credential** — create a *Postgres* credential named
   `Content Postgres` pointing at the `content` database on analytics-postgres
   (host 127.0.0.1 from the n8n container's perspective may differ — use the
   same settings as the existing `Members Postgres` credential but database
   `content`). Re-select it on both Postgres nodes.

4. **Point the admin service at this webhook.** On the VPS, set
   `PUBLISH_WEBHOOK=https://<n8n-host>/webhook/publish-article` in the
   content-admin container's environment and restart it. Until then the log
   just says `PUBLISH_WEBHOOK not set — approved but not published`.

### Why n8n owns the GitHub push

The VPS deliberately has no push access — see the diverged-branch failure in
website-build-cutover-runbook.md. n8n holds the only write token, and it can
only write file contents to one repo.

### Testing

Approve one piece at /admin/drafts/ and watch the execution. Then **approve two
at once** — the Code nodes are set to *Run Once for Each Item* on purpose, and
a single-item test cannot prove that works. This is the exact bug that hit the
lead workflow on July 31.

### Failure behaviour

If the GitHub commit fails the workflow stops there and the piece stays
APPROVED, so re-approving retries it. It does NOT get marked PUBLISHED on a
failed push — that would lose the article silently.

parameters.query:
-- Every APPROVED piece, not the ids in the request body.
--
-- The first version took the ids as a query parameter and failed silently on
-- every batch: n8n splits the Query Parameters field on commas, so "5,4"
-- arrived as $1='5' and $2='4', and a query referencing only $1 fetched one
-- piece and dropped the rest with no error. Two batches, two lost articles.
--
-- Selecting on status instead removes the parameter, and with it the bug
-- class. It also makes the webhook a trigger rather than a payload: firing it
-- twice is harmless, and a piece stranded in APPROVED by an earlier failure
-- gets picked up by the next run instead of needing a manual curl.
SELECT id, idea_id, language, slug, title, headline, short_title,
       standfirst, description, category, trans_key, reading_time, body,
       to_char(now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS pub_date
FROM content_pieces
WHERE status = 'APPROVED'
ORDER BY id;

-- NOTE: the Query Parameters field below is an ARRAY expression, not a
-- comma-joined string. n8n splits that field on commas, which is exactly what
-- broke "Load approved pieces" — see the comment there. None of the three
-- values here can contain a comma (an integer, a slug URL, a file path), so
-- this is safe, but do not add a free-text value to it without checking.
UPDATE content_pieces
SET status = 'PUBLISHED', published_at = now(),
    published_url = $2, file_path = $3
WHERE id = $1::int AND status = 'APPROVED';

UPDATE content_ideas
SET status = 'PUBLISHED', published_url = $2
WHERE id = (SELECT idea_id FROM content_pieces WHERE id = $1::int)
  AND status = 'WRITTEN';

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $('Assemble commit payload').item.json.piece_id, $('Assemble commit payload').item.json.published_url, $('Assemble commit payload').item.json.path ] }}

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, published: $('Assemble commit payload').all().map(i => i.json.path) }) }}
